candidateOutput.title: Trapping Rain Water
candidateOutput.crux: Compute total trapped water volume between N columns given heights, where water at each index depends on the maximum height to its left and right.
edgeCases: n=1 or n=2 → 0 water trapped
strictly decreasing or increasing heights → 0 water trapped
all equal heights → 0 water trapped
single tall peak with lower sides → water trapped in middle valleys
height[i] = 0 across all indices → 0 water trapped
maximum height at ends → no water trapped on outer sides
height[i] = 10^5 maximum → large water volume possible

wrongApproaches.name: Two Pointer Sum Accumulation

wrongApproaches.reason: incorrectly moves pointer based on current side max without ensuring global left/right max dominance

wrongApproaches.name: Prefix Sum of Differences

wrongApproaches.reason: maxLeft computed left-to-right misses right-side containment

wrongApproaches.name: Stack Monotonic Decreasing without Water Calculation
wrongApproaches.signal: stack pop and push, no area computation
wrongApproaches.reason: monotonic stack alone does not accumulate trapped water volume

wrongApproaches.name: Brute Force O(N^2) Left/Right Max per Index
wrongApproaches.signal: nested loops i,j computing leftMax[j] and rightMax[j]
wrongApproaches.reason: O(N^2) time exceeds limit for n up to 2*10^4

optimal.name: Two Pointers with Global Left/Right Max Tracking
optimal.keyIdea: Maintain left and right pointers with running max heights; at each step, process the side with smaller height because the water level is determined by the opposite side's max.
invariants: leftMax always reflects max height from index 0 to left pointer
rightMax always reflects max height from index n-1 to right pointer
if height[left] < height[right], process left side; else process right side
water added = min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[current] when current side processed
pitfalls: initializing leftMax/rightMax to 0 instead of height[0/right]
moving pointers based on height comparison instead of max comparison
off-by-one in loop condition while (left < right)
forgetting to add water when height[current] < min(leftMax, rightMax)

alternates.name: Prefix Max + Suffix Max Arrays
alternates.keyIdea: Precompute leftMax[i] = max height to left of i and rightMax[i] = max height to right of i; water at i = max(0, min(leftMax[i], rightMax[i]) - height[i]).
alternates.whyNotOptimal: O(N) extra space vs O(1) for two pointers, but same time complexity
recognizeBy: for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) leftMax[i] = Math.max(leftMax[i-1], height[i-1])
for (int i = n-2; i >= 0; i--) rightMax[i] = Math.max(rightMax[i+1], height[i+1])

alternates.name: Brute Force O(N^2) Column Scan

no auxiliary arrays, pure nested iteration

candidateOutput.title: The Skyline Problem
candidateOutput.crux: Compute the outer contour formed by merging overlapping rectangular buildings, outputting key points where the skyline height changes.
edgeCases: single building: [[left, height], [right, 0]]
adjacent same-height buildings: should merge into one segment, e.g. [[0,3],[5,0]] not [[0,3],[2,3],[5,0]]
buildings with zero gap between right and left edges: contiguous merging required
tall building completely shadowed by shorter ones: height contributions vanish
overlapping starts and ends at same x: process ends before starts to avoid false height spikes
coordinates up to 2^31-1: requires 64-bit integer handling for event sorting and active height tracking

wrongApproaches.reason: Coordinate range up to 2^31 makes O(range) infeasible; TLE on sparse inputs

wrongApproaches.reason: Edge handling at coincident x-values and zero-height termination often broken; misses ground between buildings

wrongApproaches.name: Priority Queue without Lazy Removal
wrongApproaches.signal: push (height, right) into heap; pop while height != top
wrongApproaches.reason: Stale right-edge entries never removed; heap top becomes invalid height that never drops

optimal.name: Line Sweep with Max-Heap and Lazy Removal
optimal.keyIdea: Convert each building into two events (start: negate height, end: positive height). Sort events by x, then by height. Sweep left-to-right, maintaining a max-heap of active heights. At each event, push start heights; for end events, lazily mark the height as expired and pop until heap top is valid. Record a key point whenever the current max height changes.
invariants: events sorted by x ascending; ties broken by height descending (start before end)
heap stores negative heights (or max-heap) with associated right x-coordinate
lazy removal: pop heap while the top's right endpoint <= current x
output only when current max height differs from previous height
pitfalls: forgetting to sort start events higher than end events at same x causes false height spikes
not implementing lazy removal leads to stale heap entries and wrong max height
neglecting to output termination point [rightmost_x, 0]
using 32-bit integers for coordinate comparisons near 2^31-1 overflow risk

candidateOutput.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
candidateOutput.crux: Find the maximum sum of any node-to-node path in a binary tree, where each node is visited at most once and the path need not include the root.
edgeCases: single node n=1 → answer is root.val
all negative values → answer is the maximum single node (least negative)
tree skewed left or right → path follows the single non-null branch
subtree sums overflow int if unchecked, but constraints limit val to [-1000,1000] and N≤3e4 → max sum 3e7 fits in 32-bit int
path entirely in left subtree, entirely in right subtree, or passes through root

wrongApproaches.name: Global DFS returning single-branch max
wrongApproaches.signal: dfs(node) returns max(node.val, node.val+left, node.val+right)
wrongApproaches.reason: Cannot combine left+right+node.val into a valid path because parent can only extend one side

wrongApproaches.name: Top-down evaluate all paths from root
wrongApproaches.signal: enumerate all root-to-node paths, compute sum, track max
wrongApproaches.reason: O(N^2) on skewed tree; misses paths not containing root

wrongApproaches.name: Two-pass diameter-style BFS
wrongApproaches.signal: BFS farthest-node twice, sum values along found path
wrongApproaches.reason: Tree diameter maximizes edges, not node values; path sum optimization differs

wrongApproaches.name: Memoized root-to-leaf sums only
wrongApproaches.signal: dp[node] = max path sum from node to any leaf
wrongApproaches.reason: Ignores paths that turn at a node, combining left and right branches

optimal.name: Post-order DFS with Global Max Tracking
optimal.keyIdea: Recursively compute the max gain from left and right children; at each node, compute priceNewPath = node.val + max(0, leftGain) + max(0, rightGain) and update global answer; return node.val + max(max(0, leftGain), max(0, rightGain)) to parent.
invariants: leftGain / rightGain are never negative (clamped to 0)
global maximum updated at every node with priceNewPath
returned value to parent is node.val + max(leftGain, rightGain) only (no both)
base case: null node returns gain 0
pitfalls: forgetting to clamp gains to 0 → including negative children reduces sum
returning left+right+node.val to parent → invalid path (node used twice)
initializing global answer to 0 → fails when all nodes negative; must init to -inf or root.val
not handling null children → null → 0 gain is correct but must be explicit

alternates.name: Brute Force Enumerate All Paths via DFS
alternates.keyIdea: Start DFS from every node, explore all downward paths, compute sum, track max.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: O(N^2) time exceeds O(N) for N up to 3*10^4
recognizeBy: outer loop over all nodes as path start
inner DFS only goes downwards (no upward then down)
no global variable updated across starts

alternates.name: Two-Global-Max DP on Tree
alternates.keyIdea: First DFS computes max downward path from each node; second DFS propagates the global max path sum that includes ancestors.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: Same O(N) time as optimal but higher constant factor and O(N) extra space for memo vs O(H) recursion

optimal.name: Tarjan's Bridge-Finding DFS (Articulation Point Variant)
optimal.keyIdea: Run one DFS maintaining discovery time `disc` and low-link `low`; an edge (u,v) is a bridge iff `low[v] > disc[u]` after processing v's subtree, because no back-edge reaches u or earlier.
invariants: `disc[u]` assigned when node u first visited, strictly increasing
`low[u]` = min(disc[u], disc[parent], low[children], disc[back-neighbors])
Bridge condition: after DFS(v) from u, if low[v] > disc[u] then (u,v) is critical
Graph is connected so single DFS root covers all nodes
pitfalls: Forgetting to skip the direct parent edge, causing false bridge on tree edges
Using `low[v] >= disc[u]` instead of `>` for articulation vs bridge confusion
Not resetting `disc`/`low` for disconnected components if graph were not guaranteed connected
Integer overflow unlikely with N=10^5 but use 32-bit int safely within limits

for neighbor v of u: if v == parent continue else if disc[v] == -1 { dfs(v); low[u] = min(low[u], low[v]); if low[v] > disc[u] add bridge } else { low[u] = min(low[u], disc[v]) }

candidateOutput.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
candidateOutput.crux: Find the maximum length of a strictly increasing sequence traversable via 4-directional moves on an m×n grid.
edgeCases: 1x1 matrix → return 1, single cell base case
strictly decreasing matrix → answer = 1, no valid moves
all equal values → answer = 1, no strictly increasing moves possible
single row or column → reduces to 1D path finding
large plateaus of same value → DFS must skip non-increasing neighbors
values at 2^31-1 max: int safe for memo dp, no overflow in additions

wrongApproaches.name: Naive DFS without memoization
wrongApproaches.signal: dfs(i,j) without visited/cache
wrongApproaches.reason: Exponential re-exploration of identical subproblems; path explores all 4^L routes, N=200 grid causes repeated full traversals from same cell

wrongApproaches.name: BFS from every cell level-by-level
wrongApproaches.signal: queue per cell, expand frontier k times
wrongApproaches.reason: Each BFS is O(N) and there are N cells; total O(N^2) with queue overhead, infeasible for 200x200 = 40K cells

wrongApproaches.name: Topological sort on grid edges
wrongApproaches.signal: Kahn's algorithm with indegree counts
wrongApproaches.reason: Longest path in DAG requires DP relaxation, not just indegree peeling; indegree approach cannot track path length accumulation correctly

wrongApproaches.name: Sort cells ascending, DP update from smaller
wrongApproaches.signal: Process cells by value, dp[nx][ny] = max(dp[nx][ny], dp[i][j]+1)
wrongApproaches.reason: Updates flow backwards: smaller→larger direction, but we need larger→smaller to accumulate path length; order of relaxation causes missing dependencies

optimal.name: DFS + Memoization (DP on DAG)
optimal.keyIdea: From each cell, recursively explore 4 neighbors with strictly greater values; cache the longest path starting at each cell in a dp[m][n] table; use visited marker to prevent recursion cycle on plateaus.
invariants: memo[i][j] stores longest increasing path starting from cell (i,j)
only transition to neighbor (nx,ny) if matrix[nx][ny] > matrix[i][j]
dp values are computed bottom-up via recursion post-order
no cycles because values strictly increase along path
pitfalls: missing base case: cell with no greater neighbors returns 1
integer overflow if adding path lengths beyond int range (mitigated by constraints)
not marking current cell temporarily to avoid re-entering same path in cycle-prone graph
forgetting to check boundary bounds before neighbor access
recognizeBy: if (nx < 0 || nx >= m || ny < 0 || ny >= n) continue

alternates.name: Topological Sort + DP (Kahn's Algorithm)
alternates.keyIdea: Reverse the direction: process cells in descending value order; for each cell, update its smaller neighbors' dp values; in-degree counts how many larger neighbors exist; when indegree hits 0, node is processed.
